newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Fifteen leftist rebels die in Colombian violence.
newsitem.headline: Fifteen leftist rebels die in Colombian violence.

text.p: Fifteen leftist rebels and a leftist politician died in the latest wave of violence to sweep Colombia, authorities said Wednesday.

They said the dead included eight National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas who were shot dead early Wednesday in northwest Choco province in an attack police blamed on regional rebel chieftain who feared the insurgents were about to desert.

In the conflict-torn banana-growing region of Uraba, in neighbouring Antioquia province, local government official Abeiro Bustamante, of the leftist Patriotic Union party (UP) was gunned down by an unidentified assassin Wednesday afternoon.

His murder came on the same day that Amnesty International issued a communique accusing the Colombian government of making hollow pledges to defend human rights in light of the killing of Bustamante's party colleague, Josue Giraldo, in an eastern province at the weekend.

Thousands of UP members have been murdered by suspected right-wing paramilitaries since the 1985 foundation of the party, said to be the political arm of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, the country's main guerrilla force.

In counterinsurgency operations in southwest Cauca province Tuesday evening, troops killed seven rebels of the Jaime Bateman guerrilla, a renegade faction of the M-19 group which laid down arms in 1990.
Anti-guerrilla operations continued Wednesday to track down other members of the group, the smallest of Colombia's guerrilla armies and not thought to number more than 100 fighters.
